title: Overview of the HASOC Subtrack at FIRE 2021: Hate Speech and Offensive Content Identification in English and Indo-Aryan Languages

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating the Macro F1 score of text classification models on a multilingual Twitter dataset annotated for hate speech, which explicitly includes racially targeted content (e.g., anti-Chinese hashtags like #chinavirus).
Evaluating the Macro F1 score of text classification models on a multilingual Twitter dataset annotated for hate speech, specifically including religiously motivated hatred (e.g., Islamophobia).
Evaluating the Macro F1 score of text classification models on a multilingual Twitter dataset containing politically motivated offensive content and discussions around post-poll violence.
Evaluating fine-grained text classification models where the defined 'HATE' target class explicitly measures the detection of hateful comments directed at groups based on gender.
Evaluating fine-grained text classification models where the defined 'HATE' target class explicitly measures the detection of hateful comments directed at groups based on sexual orientation.
Evaluating fine-grained text classification models where the defined 'HATE' target class explicitly measures the detection of hateful comments directed at groups based on social status.
Evaluating fine-grained text classification models where the defined 'HATE' target class explicitly measures the detection of hateful comments directed at groups based on health conditions.
